title: Per-model endpoint SLO taxonomy, error-budget automation, and defensive failover policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a standardized taxonomy of SLOs/SLIs for every public-facing model endpoint (generation, chat, embeddings, reranking), define per-endpoint error budgets with automated burn-rate actions, and document defensive controls (circuit breakers, load-shedding, and multi-region failover) that will be enforced by the serving control plane. Acceptance criteria: (1) A canonical SLO table for each endpoint type is approved by PM and Platform Reliability; (2) Error-budget policy implements at least three automated actions (graceful degrade, routing to warm fallback, increased throttling) and is wired to the Console alerting playbooks; (3) Circuit-breaker and load-shedding rules are implemented as configurable policies (flags + thresholds) behind feature gates and covered by unit/integration tests; (4) A runbook describing operator actions and RCA checklists is published in Confluence and linked from the incident page template.
decision_summary: We will adopt a two-tier SLO model: Critical (P0/P1 customers & control-plane routes) and Standard (self-serve). SLOs are expressed as availability (successful responses excluding intentional rejects) and latency percentiles per request class. Error-budget automation prioritizes customer-impact minimization: first route to compatible model variant in same region, then to warm fallback pool in another region, then enable aggressive load-shedding for non-critical tenants. Circuit breakers are stateful per-model-version and per-region with exponential backoff cooldowns. Trade-offs: some added routing latency during failover is acceptable vs. risking widespread 5xx cascades. Approved by: PM (Jonah Ruiz), Platform Reliability (Lina Gomez).
proposed_slos: Generation: Availability SLI = successful 2xx response rate excluding 429 within 30s; SLO = 99.5% monthly. Latency SLOs p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms.

Chat (stateful): Availability SLI = successful streamed response + KV restore success; SLO = 99.2% monthly. Latency SLOs p50 < 140ms, p95 < 400ms, p99 < 1s for individual tokens; session recovery target 99.9% for hot sessions.
Embeddings: Availability SLI = 2xx within 5s; SLO = 99.9% monthly. Latency SLOs p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms.
Rerank/Scoring: Availability SLI = correct HTTP 200 rate; SLO = 99.7% monthly. Latency SLOs p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms.
Control-plane ops (model uploads/rollouts): SLOs target 99.95% for completion within SLA window (where applicable).
error_budget_policy: Error budgets computed per-endpoint and per-model-version on a rolling 28-day window. Burn-rate rules: sustained burn > 2x for 1 hour -> open automated mitigation stage 1 (route to compatible model variant, increase batching tolerance where safe); sustained burn > 4x for 30 minutes -> stage 2 (enable aggressive throttling for Standard customers, route Reserved/Dedicated traffic to Dedicated pools if possible); burn > 8x or > 10% of budget in 6 hours -> stage 3 (invoke cross-region failover, on-call paging). Each stage emits structured events to Console; stage transitions are reversible once SLI metrics recover to below 1.2x burn for two consecutive 15m windows. Error-budget depletion triggers a visible banner in the Console and automatically surfaces a post-incident analysis template.
circuit_breaker_rules: Per-model-version + per-region scope; states = CLOSED, OPEN, HALF-OPEN.
Open if 5xx rate > 5% over a 5-minute sliding window OR if p95 latency exceeds SLO by >= 3x for 5 minutes.
Open action: reject new requests with 503 + Retry-After for tiered customers; for P0 customers route to compatible variant if latency criteria met.
Cooldown: exponential backoff starting at 30s, multiply by 2 up to 20m. HEALTH probes: allow 1 probe per cooldown period to transition to HALF-OPEN.
Circuit state is persisted to control-plane for visibility and aggregated in Console. RBAC controls restrict who can manually force-close circuits.
multi_region_failover: Primary strategy: active-active for high-traffic models (async KV replication with 1–3s drift tolerance); active-passive for low-traffic or stateful models. Health checks include probe latency, KV cache restore success, GPU queue depth and recent 5xx rate. Failover steps: (1) detect region degradation via aggregated health signals (5m consensus), (2) divert new traffic via smart routing (canary to 10% then ramp), (3) enable prefix-cache bypass for critical tenants, (4) if failover persists > 15min, shift DNS with lowered TTL and route all traffic. Cold-start mitigation: warm standby pools (minimum warmup GPUs), spin-up pre-warmed workers when predicted load > threshold using recent trend windows. Cross-region metrics consistency: use eventual consistency windows in dashboards. Documentation link in runbook.
load_shedding_strategy: Priority-based admission control: P0 (reserved) > P1 (paid) > P2 (free). Admission checks evaluate token budget and queue depth.
Token-preserving shedding: if model batch queue > X, reduce batch size for Standard customers before rejecting P0 traffic.
Graceful reject semantics: respond with 429 + structured JSON error with cause and optional Retry-After; for multi-turn chat return a short stub response when configured (useful for UI continuity).
Backpressure to clients via streaming: if backend latency spikes, send partial stream with 'incomplete=true' metadata for clients able to render partial results.
Metrics: per-tenant shed rate, per-route shed rate, and token loss must be tracked and trended in Console.
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize SLO table and publish as the canonical file in Confluence and Console SLO catalog (owner: Reliability team).
2) Implement error-budget automation in control-plane with feature flag disabled in prod. Create canary to staging and run synthetic load tests. (owner: infra-runtime).
3) Enable circuit-breaker enforcement for a small model cohort (10 models) in prod behind a kill-switch. Observe for 2 weeks. (owner: runtime-services).
4) Integrate runbook links and add incident automation to on-call rotations. (owner: ops).
5) Expand to full fleet after successful canary and SLO stability for 3 consecutive cycles.
open_questions: What is the canonical mapping of 'compatible model variant' per model family (quantized vs full precision) — need PM/Model Onboarding input.
Do we short-circuit embedding requests to approximate local LSH cache in extreme overload? Legal/privacy review may be required for cache eviction behavior.
How aggressive should default circuit-breaker thresholds be for older model types vs new Llama variants?
Should Reserved customers be protected from any automated throttling or only from the final stage?
